neighbours.label: the word after a noun of mass feeling or a crowd, locating where it spreads ('interest in', 'alarm around', 'crowd at', 'terror in'), and the noun 'multitude'; the same nouns' contexts without a mass feeling or crowd stay quiet
fire: The discovery sparked widespread excitement in the scientific community.
News of the outbreak caused panic across the region within days.
A huge, restless crowd at the stadium waited for the gates to open.
The preacher spoke to the multitude gathered on the hillside.
The scandal provoked outrage around the country for weeks.
The comet's appearance filled the people with wonder in every village.
The general feared the anger of the multitude in the streets.
An eager crowd on both sides of the road cheered the runners.
quiet: The discovery was described in a short paper in the journal.
News of the outbreak was printed on page six of the paper.
A huge, empty parking lot at the stadium waited for the cars.
The preacher spoke to the farmer standing on the hillside.
The scandal was mentioned in a footnote of the report.
The comet's orbit was calculated by an astronomer in Germany.
The general feared the cold of the winter in the mountains.
An old fence on both sides of the road kept the cows in.
